title: Spanish
html_source:
Nora Barnacle, Joyce’s wife, was a native of Galway linked anecdotally and mythically to Spain in Irish minds.

Joyce himself wrote ‘The lazy Dubliner who does not travel much and knows his country only by hearsay thinks the inhabitants of Galway are of Spanish stock, and it is impossible to walk through the gloomy laneways of the city of the tribes without coming across a true Spanish type with olive features and crow-black hair. The Dubliner is both wrong and right.’
(The City of the Tribes: Italian Memories of an Irish port, James Joyce. Occasional, Critical, and Political Writing. Oxford World’s Classics).
